Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:49: And therefore a person must repair his soul so that it be a throne for YHVH, the Cause of causes, to rest in it, and therefore he must do this out of love, so as to be cleaved to Him. And so it is written in Sefer Chassidim (section 73), that one of the things that hinders prayer from being heard is if he is not pure; and according to the view of the Tosafot (Chullin 122b, s.v. "le-gabel"), who hold that immersion is required for prayer but not for Torah - there is good reason for this along the secret path, and it is correct in practice: for the Torah, because of its abundant virtue, being in the world of the male, has the power to withstand the husk and does not receive impurity, like fire. But prayer is a request for mercy and supplication, requiring intention of the heart, and while impure his intention will certainly be confused - and therefore one must be careful about it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:50: And in the secret of the mikveh, it is already known what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas) and in the Tikkunim (page 39a), that it is in the secret of the supernal, nine points on each side, and so on - see there. And the secret of the mikveh is the secret of YHVH - for the mikveh contains forty se'ah, and YHVH likewise has four letters, each letter comprising ten - and this is the secret of "the Mikveh of Israel is YHVH" (Jeremiah 17:13) - understand this concerning what they said (Yoma, chapter 8, mishnah 9): just as a mikveh purifies the impure, so the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies Israel - namely, the purification of their souls, which are cleaved to His Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:51: It follows that one who immerses is truly cleaved to YHVH, to purify his body and his soul - his body in the water, and his soul in the spirituality of the Name resting there. And through this no harm will befall him, even if the water is cold, for since he is cleaved to YHVH, it is impossible for harm to come to him - as the Psalmist said (Psalms 91:2), "I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress," and so on, "for He shall deliver you from the snare of the fowler," meaning cold and traps. And so the rest of the psalm: "for He shall give His angels charge over you," and so on, "they shall bear you up in their hands, lest you dash your foot against a stone," and the rest of the psalm.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:52: However, one must perform the commandment with joy, for if he does not serve with joy he is punished, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:53: And it is also proper to contemplate repentance, for repentance is in the secret of the mikveh, and likewise the soul flows from there - and when a person sins, repentance departs, and likewise the soul departs from the person, and he is far from cleaving. And through the person's entering the mikveh, which is a squared "mem" [40 se'ah] - Imma who broods over the building - the Mother, who is repentance [teshuvah], "returns" [tashuv], the heh-vav returning and crouching over the children - so too the soul shall return to the person, and the Cause of causes shall rest upon his soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:54: And I heard from a certain elder sage that one who is impure - the soul does not rest in him until he enters the mikveh, and this is so for the reason I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:55: And the reason for the soul's departure is that, because of its extreme subtlety, any blemished aspect found in the body prevents it from resting there, until it returns to the source of the soul and is included there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:56: And this matter a person must intend in his immersion: that he enters, in the secret of his soul, into those supernal waters, which are in the secret of the World to Come, and he is hidden in the supernal hiding place, which is in Binah, and Imma hides him beneath her wings - and just as it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 39a) that the Shechinah immerses and is purified in the waters of the mikveh, so certainly Ze'ir Anpin immerses; and so he should intend that he ascends there in the secret of the vav, and his spirit and soul are purified from all blemish. And he should also intend that the spark of the Shechinah clothed within him is likewise purified from the blemish it received - and through the immersion he strips off the spirit of impurity from himself and the secret of the departed soul is reclothed in him. And immersion is a great aid to the acquisition of the soul, for purity is from within and holiness from without - see what I explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:57: And you already know that the law is that the water must be such that "all his flesh goes up in them" (Pesachim 109a) - meaning that they cover him entirely, and no part of him remains outside the water, even the breadth of a hair; for since the external element retains a foothold at some limb, however small, from there its impurity spreads to all the limbs, and it is as though he had not immersed at all. But when he immerses and all 248 of his limbs enter the forty se'ah, he has stripped from himself every aspect of the spirit of impurity, for it is within the power of Imma to nullify the external forces, since she is the great eagle with the wings that does not fear the swooping hawk and the like.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:58: And a further reason: immersion in the mikveh is like the return of vessels to the furnace to be purified and refined, and upon their emergence from the furnace they are new. So too a person, in entering the mikveh, is in order to be included and to return the blemished soul and the blemished limbs to the place from which they came - and there they become hidden, like a fetus hidden in its mother's womb, over whom the external eye has no rule, and he is guarded from every mishap and accident, as they explained, of blessed memory (Niddah 30b), "as in the days when God watched over me" (Job 29:2), referring to a child in its mother's womb. And upon the person's emerging from the mikveh, his limbs and his soul have been repaired, and he is new, and the external forces have no part in him - and the person will feel within himself a new spirit from the spark of the soul that has returned to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:59: And it is fitting that before he enters the mikveh he contemplate repentance for his iniquities, and if possible also confess, so that no portion remains to the external forces in the soul. And the matter is clear: for just as, in purifying oneself from ordinary impurity - a seminal emission, a flow, and the like - nothing must intervene between him and the water, for the reason I explained, so too concerning the purification of iniquity, which is a more spiritual impurity, cleaving to the soul until it causes it a blemish and darkening, requiring a washing to remove it with lye and soap through repentance - nothing should intervene from within, in his soul. For it has already been explained that the essence of immersion for a penitent is to purify himself from his iniquities and to restore the soul to him - if so, he must set his heart to this: to turn from his iniquities entirely, and not immerse while some of his iniquities still remain in his hand, for the immersion will not avail him for the purification of his iniquities, as explained, until he abandons them completely and entirely. And this is along the lines of what will be explained, with God's help, concerning repentance: that the matter of prayer and requesting forgiveness for iniquity requires that he first repair, as far as it is in his power, from his iniquities, and only afterward pray about them - and therefore it is fitting that he confess before entering the mikveh, or at least contemplate it. And in Sefer Chassidim they wrote that it is fitting to immerse three times, corresponding to sin, iniquity, and transgression.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:60: And when the mikveh water is cold and he suffers, he should intend what they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 5a), that the World to Come is attained only through suffering, which is one of the three good gifts the Holy One, blessed be He, gave to Israel - and immersion is an allusion to the World to Come, and therefore requires suffering. And by accepting upon himself the aspect of cold, which is the judgment flowing from Gevurah, he merits the light of life, the good hidden away above in the World to Come - and this is (Proverbs 6:23), "and the way of life is the reproofs of discipline" - meaning, it is [an aspect of] mercy. And so you find (Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, page 247a) that souls do not enter the supernal Garden of Eden until they immerse in the River of Fire.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:61: And one who is careful to perform the immersion at its proper time will certainly not be reached by any harmful force, for "one who guards a commandment shall know no evil thing" - but if he is prevented by circumstance beyond his control from performing it in its time, [that is one matter]; but if he is negligent in the commandment without any such prevention, it is possible that the commandment will not protect him from the mishaps of the time. And if he was negligent in performing it at its proper time, let him hasten to repent, and not allow the impurity to grow old in his soul, for afterward it will be hard to separate it - along the lines of what is written (Zohar, Parashat Pinchas, page 227b), "before old age you shall rise" (Leviticus 19:32 [sic]) - before the evil inclination grows old in him. And let him trust in the LORD, for one who comes to purify himself is assisted, and no harm shall befall him - for the reason explained, that in purifying himself he also purifies his soul and spirit, which are a supernal portion, and since he purifies portions of the holy sparks, he is certainly assisted.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:62: And one must think, in performing this commandment, of fear and love, just as is needed in general for the commandments, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 10, page 25b) - fear, that he not be negligent in performing it, and that he fear the supernal King who commands it, and it is fitting not to transgress His will; and he should think, were a king of flesh and blood to command this, how careful he would be to perform it, not to transgress the king's command. And from the side of love, that he desire love of the King - for it is fitting, out of love for Him, that even were He to command him to cast himself into a fiery furnace, like Abraham, he would throw himself in; all the more so since all the King's commandments are for our benefit, to give us an inheritance of a world that is wholly long [everlasting], as he says (Deuteronomy 6:25), "and it shall be righteousness for us, if we observe to do."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:63: And even in this world he has good reward for his effort, as they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 22b), that its virtue is length of days, in these words: Rabbi Yannai said, I have heard that some are strict about it, and I have heard that some are lenient about it - and whoever is strict about it upon himself, his days and years are lengthened - to this point. And the reason is that its secret is in the place of length of life, namely "al Hashem" [upon the LORD], as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei, page 79b), and the first three [sefirot] are considered as one. Also, one who performs the commandment with a desire like his desire for life - for it concerns the commandment that is YHVH, the source of life, and he is cleaved to the Cause of causes, cleaved to YHVH - certainly he will lengthen his days through this intention of his.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:64: And he must be joyful in performing the commandment, like one who goes to earn much money and is joyful about it - so he should be joyful in the commandments, for he is cleaved to His great Name YHVH and to the supernal life, and he repairs his soul; and as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:162), "I rejoice at Your word, as one who finds great spoil," and it says (Habakkuk 3:18), "yet I will exult in the LORD."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:65: And concerning the plain sense of Rabbi Yannai's saying, Rashi explained that "some are lenient about it" means in bathhouses or by pouring nine kav [of water]; "some are strict about it" means in forty se'ah. And the Tosafot wrote that even though they said in the Gemara that they abolished the requirement of immersion, following Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, that was specifically for Torah study, but for prayer it is still required.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:66: And the students of Rabbenu Yonah wrote concerning this matter, what they said there in the Gemara, which Rav Alfasi, peace be upon him, brought: words of Torah do not receive impurity, as it is said, "is not My word like fire," and so on. They said, of blessed memory, that some explain that there is no difference between the Shema and other reading - for all matters we say that words of Torah do not receive impurity - but this is not correct, for certainly they said this only concerning the Shema alone, but concerning other words of Torah it is forbidden, for they said (Numbers 15:31), "for he has despised the word of the LORD," and so on - this refers to one who reads words of Torah in filthy alleyways - and they were stricter about this than about other matters punishable by karet [excision], for in all other cases of karet, the karet itself atones, but in this case it does not atone, even though his iniquity is cut off through it - to this point. Behold, according to their words, Torah is more severe than prayer, and one who reads Torah in impurity, his body being impure, is more severe than one who reads Torah in filthy alleyways, for which there is a punishment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:67: Further they wrote afterward, that Rav Alfasi wrote, and Rabbenu Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, wrote, that since there is no explicit Talmudic ruling on this matter, follow the custom of all Israel, that all who have had a seminal emission, even if they have no water, do not pray until they have washed. And they wrote there that this washing is not in forty se'ah but in nine kav, and the nine kav must be poured upon him from a vessel that can pour them upon him without any interruption. And this is also proven from the Mishnayot of Tohorot (Mikva'ot, chapter 3, mishnayot 3-4). What the Gaon, of blessed memory, wrote, that one does not pray until he has washed, did not seem correct to my teacher the Rabbi, may his light shine, and if he has no water, or even if he has water but does not immerse or wash, even so he does not lose his prayer because of this - for certainly, even though prayer is more acceptable with immersion according to all opinions, he should not lose his prayer because of this. And so Rabbenu Moshe [Maimonides], of blessed memory, wrote that all the heads of the academies in Babylonia wondered at him, why he was so lenient concerning the immersions of one who had a seminal emission - and he, of blessed memory, answered them that he had never abolished it, but that he could only write in his compilation what follows from the law according to the halachah - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:68: And the words of Rabbenu Yonah on this follow his own view, which he wrote, that words of Torah are more severe than prayer - and therefore he will not omit prayer so as not to let its time pass, but words of Torah, according to his view, he will not read.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:69: And I say, that one who fears Heaven should fulfill all views: when his body is found healthy, let him be strict, with forty se'ah; and if his body is weak, or in the cold days, let him pour upon himself nine kav of warm water. In any case, if he is prevented by circumstance and immersion is not available to him, he should not, because of this, omit either Torah or prayer, for those who are lenient are fit to be relied upon in a time of pressing need. And at night, before he has immersed, he should not refrain from rising in the night watch to occupy himself with Torah because he is impure, for the other decisors are fit to be relied upon. A person should not be idle from words of Torah, and should consider those hours like a day when he is ill, when certainly he would not omit Torah and prayer - and whoever is strict upon himself not to occupy himself with Torah and prayer without immersion, even when he is ill, holds a strange view, and it is not fitting to rely upon it. And as I have written, this was the practice of our teacher Rabbi Isaac Luria Ashkenazi, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:70: Further we find in the Torah that all of a person's purification, whether from his impurity or from his soiling, and the washing of his garments, is all in water, as it is written (Leviticus 14:9), "and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and be pure," and likewise (ibid. 13:6), "and he shall wash his clothes, and be pure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:71: Further, purity is found concerning garments, as Jacob our father, peace be upon him, said when he wished to come to Beth-El (Genesis 35:2), "purify yourselves, and change your garments." And although these appear to be two separate things - the first, "purify yourselves" through immersion, and further, "and change your garments" - nevertheless, since he placed them together, the change of garments is a species of purification; and it is fitting for one who wishes to purify himself that his garments be pure of soiling and impurity, and not soiled with oil, grease, and the like - for they explained (Shabbat 114a) that a Torah scholar found with a grease stain on his garments is liable to death, as it is said (Proverbs 8:36), "all who hate me love death" - do not read "those who hate me" [mesan'ai] but "those who cause hatred of me" [mas'ni'ai].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:72: And so the Rokeach, peace be upon him, wrote concerning the root of purity: be careful about the purity of your garments, that your clothes not be soiled with excrement or drops of urine. "Keep your feet when you go to the house of God" - therefore train yourself to wipe well; guard your orifices, and do not accustom yourself to urinate close to the redemption blessing, lest it drip onto your trousers - how can you pray "forgive us, for we have sinned," while you stand soiled? And be careful about seminal emission, lest it cling to your flesh and your garments; and let your garments not be among the ornaments of idolatry. "Purify yourself, prepare to meet your God, O Israel" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:73: Further, purity is found concerning place, as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said to Aaron (Leviticus 10:14), "and the thigh of the offering you shall eat in a pure place." And Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Terumah (page 128a), in the discourse we copied in chapter 5, said: and the spirit of holiness is not so, but [requires] a whole wage, and the repair of oneself, and the purification of his dwelling. Behold, "the purification of his dwelling" - the purity of the place; and "the repair of oneself" - meaning, "prepare to meet your God, O Israel." And without doubt this preparation is also through immersion, as the Rokeach wrote.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:74: Further, in the purification of the leper, we find, as part of his purification, the shaving of the hair, as it is written (Leviticus 14:9), "the one being purified shall wash his clothes, and shave off all his hair" - and the reason is that the hair of the head, in the young, are the forces of judgment, and it is good to shave them, along the lines of (cf. Zohar, Parashat Vayechi, page 217a), "before this head of his Master is revealed" - and this is the secret of (Leviticus 13:40), "and if a man's hair has fallen from his head, he is bald, he is pure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:75: And so it is good, for purification, to cut the nails - for the woman purifying herself for her husband must cut them, as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei Mot (79a) and Parashat Pinchas (248b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:76: Further, one must purify oneself from all the things concerning which impurity is mentioned in the Torah and in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory - and I have already copied most of them in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5, and there are further particulars that will be explained below, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:77: And the essence of purity is what was explained above: that he purify himself from every iniquity and guilt, as it is written (Ezekiel 36:25), "and I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall be pure; from all your impurities and from all your idols I will purify you" - certainly this refers to the purification of the evil inclination, from whose side the essence of impurity comes, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 51:4), "and purify me from my sin," and many similar verses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:78: And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 17a): it was a common saying in the mouth of Rabbi Meir - study with all your heart and with all your soul to know all My ways, and to be diligent at the doors of My Torah; guard My Torah in your heart, and let My fear be before your eyes; guard your mouth from all sin, and purify yourself from all guilt and iniquity - and I shall be with you in every place - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:79: And a person must intend to purify his iniquities through drawing down the supernal light from the place of whiteness, in his intention of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy - and especially in two of them in which the purification of iniquities and their whitening is mentioned: in the second attribute, "who forgives iniquity," it says in the Idra of Naso (page 132b), "and one that was dark, was washed in that light, like one washed in that deep river." And in the third attribute, "who passes over transgression," they said there (page 133a), that of this it is said (Job 37:21), "and a wind passed and purified them." And although all thirteen attributes have the virtue of sweetening judgments, in these two in particular the matter of purification is mentioned, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:80: Especially on the Day of Atonement, which is a day of atonement to purify iniquities, as it is written (Leviticus 16:30), "for on this day He shall atone for you, to purify you from all your sins" - one must intend what has been said: that the Day of Atonement is above, and Arich Anpin is revealed to purify and whiten our iniquities - and this is "before the LORD you shall be purified."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:81: Further, purity is found concerning the hands, as he says (Job 17:9), "and he who has clean [tahor] hands shall grow stronger" - and what we explained above concerning "clean hands" is "turning from evil" [sur me-ra]; but the "purity" mentioned here is for fulfillment and "doing good" [aseh tov] - meaning, that he occupy his hands with the commandments of tzitzit, tefillin, sukkah, and lulav, and the like. And as to why it is expressed in terms of "purity" - for "purity" also seems to indicate turning from evil - the meaning of "purity" here is only the sense of brightness of light, along the lines of (Exodus 24:10), "and it was like the very heaven for clearness [la-tohar]" - and "tohar" is the palace of Nogah; and so the language of our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Chullin 60b), "of what use is a lamp at noon [be-tihara]?" And it is impossible for a person to attain brightness of light through turning from evil alone, but rather through his occupation with the commandments, supernal light in the World to Come is added to his hand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:82: Further, we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "of purer eyes than to behold evil" (Habakkuk 1:13) - and following the way we said concerning "clean hands," we must say that it is not only that He does not see evil, but He is pure in that His providence is always in holiness, for He is holy and His ministers are holy. And the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "of pure eyes," in that His providence always stands in its brightness and does not spread to the external forces - and it is impossible to say of the Holy One, blessed be He, Heaven forfend, "of clean eyes," which would suggest He saw evil and needed cleansing - rather He always stands in His purity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:83: However, according to what is explained in the Idra of Naso concerning the eye of Arich [Anpin], where he says (page 130a), we have learned, there is no light for the lower eye to be washed from redness, from blackness, except when it sees that this white light is of the supernal eye, which is called "the good eye" - to this point - it follows that "purity" is according to its plain meaning: that the eyes be purified from the redness of judgment, through the illumination of supernal light from the eye of Arich.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:84: And we can say that both are true - for in being purified from judgment through the supernal light, brightness of light is added to them; and the word "purity" is used in Scripture in these two senses - either the purification of a blemished thing so that it remains in its previous whiteness, as it was, or the addition of illumination, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:85: And a person must liken himself to his Creator, to purify his eyes from seeing evil, as will be explained in the repair of the eyes - and especially not to gaze upon the image of a wicked person, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Megillah 28a): Rabbi Ami asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah, to what do you attribute your length of days? He said to him, in all my days I never gazed upon the image of a wicked person. And everything that causes length [of days] depends on Arich Anpin - it follows that the supernal eye does not gaze upon the wicked, as explained above, and this is "of purer eyes than to behold evil."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:86: However, he should liken himself to his Creator by gazing upon everything of holiness - for just as His providence, blessed be He, is to flow to the holy, as it is written (Psalms 33:18), "behold, the eye of the LORD is upon those who fear Him" - and through this he causes the eye of Arich Anpin to shine into the eyes of Ze'ir [Anpin]. And it appears good to intend this when gazing upon something of holiness, and he will merit in the future that "eye to eye they shall see, when the LORD returns to Zion" (Isaiah 52:8) - and so they said there (Zohar, Parashat Naso, page 130a), and the righteous, the supernal meritorious ones, are destined to see with wisdom - this is what is written, "for eye to eye they shall see" - when? "when the LORD returns to Zion" - and it is written (Numbers 14:14), "that You, LORD, are seen eye to eye" - to this point. And without doubt none merit this level except the righteous who guarded their eyes properly, as they said, "the righteous, the supernal meritorious ones."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:87: Further, we find in "purity" a great matter relevant to practice, namely what they explained, of blessed memory (Yoma 72b), on the verse (Psalms 19:10), "the fear of the LORD is pure" - in these words: Rabbi Yochanan said, this refers to one who studies Torah in purity. What is that? He marries a wife and afterward studies Torah - to this point. And without doubt, in order for a person to attain the cleaving of his thought to his God, he must first marry a wife, and through this his thoughts will be purified - for without a wife it is impossible for him to attain any completeness, since he is lacking and blemished, a possessor of a defect; certainly, when he is married he is a complete person, as it is said (Genesis 5:2), "male and female He created them, and called their name Adam" - as they elaborated in Parashat Vayikra (7b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:88: Further, purity is found concerning the table: "upon the pure table" (2 Chronicles 13:11). And although this concerns the matter of law, that it is called "pure," as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 26b), nevertheless the Torah is expounded in several ways, and we can say that "pure" is written to teach a person moral discipline, that his table be pure - meaning, that he not be drawn after bodily pleasures that come from the side of the evil inclination, for a person's table is called an altar, to atone for him - and when he is not drawn after the pleasures of his inclination, certainly through this he subdues his inclination, and it becomes an altar of atonement to purify his iniquities.
